newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hostage-taker holds six in German bank.
newsitem.headline: Hostage-taker holds six in German bank.

text.p: A man took six hostages at a bank in southwestern Germany on Friday and threatened to shoot them unless he received a ransom of five million marks ($3 million), police said on Friday.

His deadline for police to meet his demands passed at 10 p.m. local time (2000 GMT) without reporters near the bank in the small town of Neuenstein, near Heidelberg, hearing or seeing anything out of the ordinary.

The man seized the hostages in the small town of Neuenstein, near Heidelberg, in the late afternoon. He also demanded a getaway car and said he would shoot the hostages if anyone went near the building.
A local radio station said the man had telephoned its office three times. He said one hostage would be shot every hour if police did not respect his deadline, Radio Regenbogen reported.
In the third call, a loud bang could be heard after an interviewer asked him what weapons he had. The caller said he had not shot anyone but was just proving he was armed.
He said he was holding four bank employees, a cleaner and a customer.
Police sealed off the area around the bank and asked nearby residents not to leave their homes.
